title: Prism: first install
summary: PhotoPrism on the old PC, read-only and house network only: browse and search the photos already in the house share from a laptop or phone. Mark installed when it works.

start.body: Prism here means PhotoPrism: a photo library you run. It reads the photo folder you already copy into and gives you a timeline, search and a map in the browser. One container plus a database, house network only.

fit.body: Pick it if the files are the library and you want a nicer way to browse them. This walkthrough runs it read-only: it can look at the house share but never change it. Want automatic phone upload and face search on day one? That is Immich.

choices.label: I already run it — mark Prism and photos installed

prereq.body:
You need the old PC on Debian or Ubuntu Server, SSH from the couch, a house share with photos in it, and at least 2 CPU cores, 3 GB of RAM and 4 GB of swap. Check from SSH:

```
free -h
df -h /srv/share
```

The Swap line should say at least 4.0G.

need-docker.body:
Download Docker's script, read it, then run it:

```
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com -o ~/get-docker.sh
less ~/get-docker.sh
sudo sh ~/get-docker.sh
```

Check that Compose answers with a version number:

```
sudo docker compose version
```

download.body:
Make a folder for PhotoPrism, download its official Compose file and open it:

```
mkdir ~/photoprism && cd ~/photoprism
wget https://dl.photoprism.app/docker/compose.yaml
nano compose.yaml
```

edit.body:
All settings live in this one file. Change: PHOTOPRISM_ADMIN_PASSWORD to a real password, 8 characters or more. PHOTOPRISM_SITE_URL to the PC's address, like "http://192.168.1.50:2342/". PHOTOPRISM_DATABASE_PASSWORD and MARIADB_PASSWORD to the same new password, and MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD too. PHOTOPRISM_READONLY to "true". Under volumes, change ~/Pictures:/photoprism/originals to /srv/share:/photoprism/originals.

Keep the indentation. Set the passwords before the first start: the database keeps its first one. Save with Ctrl+O, Enter, Ctrl+X.

up.body:
Start it and check both containers:

```
sudo docker compose up -d
sudo docker compose ps
```

Wait until photoprism and mariadb both say Up. If the page won't load later, read the log:

```
sudo docker compose logs photoprism --tail 50
```

web.body:
On a laptop on house Wi-Fi, open http://192.168.1.50:2342 with your own address and sign in as admin. Forgot the password after the first start? Editing the file won't help; in ~/photoprism run:

```
sudo docker compose exec photoprism photoprism passwd admin
```

index.body: Go to Library, then Index, and press Start. On an old PC the first pass over a big folder can take hours; let it run overnight. When new photos land in the share later, press Start again.

empty.body:
An empty library usually means the originals line points at the wrong folder. Check what PhotoPrism sees:

```
sudo docker compose exec photoprism ls /photoprism/originals
```

If your folders are missing, fix the volumes line in compose.yaml, run sudo docker compose up -d, and index again.

phone.body: On the same house Wi-Fi, open the same address in the phone's browser and sign in. Browse, search and the map all work there. The phone still adds photos by copying the camera roll to the share, then you index again; read-only mode turns off PhotoPrism's own uploads on purpose.

Still wrestling — keep Prism as interested

keep.body:
Keep it on the house network: don't forward port 2342. Your photos are already covered by the house-folder backup; copy PhotoPrism's own folder too so you don't have to re-index:

```
sudo rsync -a ~/photoprism/storage/ /mnt/backup/photoprism-storage/
```

To update later, read the release notes, then in ~/photoprism:

```
sudo docker compose pull && sudo docker compose up -d
```

stuck.body: Usual causes: the wrong address, a container not Up (sudo docker compose ps), or the log naming a bad line in compose.yaml (sudo docker compose logs photoprism --tail 50). Replay this walkthrough when you are ready.

interested.body: Noted. Replay this walkthrough when you have an evening. Keep it on the house network when you do.

installed.body: Good. Leave read-only mode on and don't point Prism and Immich at the same folder until you have picked one.

skip.body: Fine. Immich or plain folder backup still cover most houses.
